disease_label_per_paper: Left renal abscess in a healthy young female with no risk factors
presentation_summary: 21-year-old previously healthy woman presented with four days of left flank pain, fever, nausea, and dysuria, with two days of vomiting.
She had no history of UTI, renal stones, vesicoureteral reflux, genitourinary anatomic abnormality, pregnancy, immunocompromise, sexual activity, or other medical conditions.
Admission observations: temperature 37.8 C, blood pressure 91/64 mmHg, heart rate 82/min, respiratory rate 14/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air; highest day-one temperature was 39 C.
Examination was unremarkable except mild left upper quadrant tenderness.
Admission labs showed CRP 196 mg/L, WBC 17.3 x 10^9/L with neutrophil predominance, and slightly raised creatinine 89 umol/L.

Blood and urine cultures showed no growth. Persistent daily fever despite IV amoxicillin and gentamicin prompted imaging; ultrasound suggested an expanded upper calyx with clot/debris, and MRI confirmed a left renal abscess with reactive hepatosplenomegaly, bilateral pleural effusions, and small intraperitoneal fluid.

microbiology.result: Gram-positive cocci in clusters; methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus sensitive to flucloxacillin
microbiology.source_text_value: drained pus grew gram-positive cocci in clusters; it was methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), sensitive to flucloxacillin

procedures.source_text_value: ultrasound-guided drain was placed into the left upper pole of a kidney with a pigtail on day 10 of illness, day six of admission

clinical_course.event: Presumed urinary tract infection; started IV amoxicillin and gentamicin as per hospital microbial guidelines.
Continued daily temperature spikes despite IV antibiotics, raising concern for resistance or alternative diagnosis and prompting microbiology consultation and renal ultrasound.
Drainage sample grew MSSA sensitive to flucloxacillin; no further fever spikes after drainage and inflammatory markers came down significantly.
Creatinine returned to normal and she recovered well after discharge.

actual_treatment: ultrasound-guided pigtail drainage of left upper-pole renal abscess
oral flucloxacillin for two weeks after discharge
planned repeat imaging in two to three months

outcome.source_text_value: creatinine was back to normal; discharged with oral flucloxacillin; she has since recovered well
